gaps.sentence: He ___ to the reporters that the deal was off.
gaps.explanation: 'Said to the reporters that...' is correct; tell cannot be followed by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw the accident happen,' the witness stated. The witness stated that he ___ the accident happen.
gaps.explanation: Past simple backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb: saw → had seen.

gaps.sentence: 'Which seat do you prefer?' the steward asked. The steward asked which seat I ___.
gaps.explanation: do you prefer → I preferred: statement order, present simple backshifted.

gaps.sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you ever been to Iceland?' she asked. She asked ___ ever been to Iceland.
gaps.explanation: Have you been → if I had been: if/whether with past perfect.

gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
